mainEntity.name: What is a cybersecurity PR agency and who is it for?

acceptedAnswer.text: A cybersecurity PR agency runs media strategy for security companies: threat intelligence vendors, zero-trust platforms, DePIN security layers, AI governance tools and enterprise security startups. The job is to get the right story into the right US outlets at the right moment so buyers, investors and Gartner analysts find you when they are forming their vendor shortlists. For most Series A and Series B security founders, a fractional senior operator delivers sharper results than a large agency because the person building your press relationships is the person who knows your product.

mainEntity.name: How much does cybersecurity PR cost in the US market?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traditional US cybersecurity PR agencies commonly charge $15K–$45K per month to fund a multi-person account team. A fractional senior operator covers the same senior-level scope for $5K–$12K per month. A focused launch sprint, typically four to eight weeks around a product release, raise announcement or RSA Conference moment, runs $15K–$40K as a project fee.

mainEntity.name: Which outlets and analysts can you actually reach?

acceptedAnswer.text: US security press: Dark Reading, SC Media, The Register, Wired, TechCrunch Security, SecurityWeek, Infosecurity Magazine and Forbes. Mainstream where the angle warrants: Bloomberg, Wall Street Journal, Yahoo Finance. Industry analysts: Gartner, Forrester and IDC briefings coordinated to align with your coverage cycle. Coverage depends on a real news hook tied to a named threat trend, a funding event, a significant product milestone or a data-backed research angle.

mainEntity.name: What does the timeline look like from start to first placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first two weeks cover narrative teardown and category framing. Weeks three and four produce the pitch assets: a tight media brief, a short research angle if needed, and the journalist and analyst target list. Outreach begins in week five, with first placements typically landing in weeks six to ten depending on the news hook strength and the outlet. For a major product launch or funding announcement with an embargo strategy, coordinated placements can land in a single news cycle.
